# Playtest diary: r10-typed-full

- **Mode:** typed
- **Start:** the start of the game
- **Persona:** a retired librarian who reads the manual first and maps every room on graph paper
- **Seed:** 5461
- **Conveniences:** on
- **Undo:** off
- **Build commit:** d330802
- **Budget:** about 400 commands per leg, 1500 commands in all
- **Round:** 10
- **Friction log:** filed through the harness (--friction), in playtests/2026-09-27/r10-typed-full.friction.jsonl

## Narrative

### Commands 0
Session created. Opening at Deck Twelve, score 0. As a librarian I'd like to read the package papers first (the harness lets me view them with --paper). Plan: read the Assignment Completion Form, then map methodically. Memory note: I vaguely recall from the 1987 box that the goal is to get to the station and that Floyd returns; I'll only act on what the screen tells me.


### Commands 1-14
Read QX-17-T (assignment: spacetruck from Deck Five cargo bay; ID 1451-352-716; course chart time->course, noted in my scratch) and JZ-59-G (robot pool "Deck Five"). Game time moves ~22 per move. Mapped Deck Twelve (slot by port door), Forms Storage Room aft (dead end, boxes), Cargo Bay Entrance starboard, Robot Pool fore of it. Put robot form in slot, typed 3: Floyd (recognised from Planetfall memory, confirmed on screen) joined. Cargo Bay starboard of entrance has a spacetruck, hatch closed. Odd: forms say Deck Five but I'm on Deck Twelve and this all worked.

### Commands 15-30
Opened hatch, entered spacetruck, took survival kit (orange goo, gray goo, Thermos). Activation form refused until both seats filled; sat in pilot seat, Floyd took copilot. Inserted HB-56-V, typed 328 from the chart (time 5133 in 5100-5149). Waited ~6 turns: fuel warnings, braking, docking bay one occupied so bay two, "Stationfall." +5. Hungry and thirsty now. No one to meet us.

### Commands 31-50
Ate orange goo (apricot yogurt). Drink refused: "neither hungry nor thirsty... in about 319 moves" - helpful hint. Left truck. Station Level Five lobby (E elevator+call button, NE/SE corridor, N and W doors, ladder up/down). N: Workshop (twenty-ohm bedistor, taken); N of that: Storage, pitch dark. NE from lobby: North Junction (corridor N, door E, doorway NE). E: Sick Bay with ID-reader security door east (my ID card: "Nothing happens"). SE: East Connection (iris hatch to Military Sub-Module, slot). S: Comm Center, beacon button, blank screen. Plato the robot joined; knows little ("ask about station" -> library).

### Commands 51-77
Plato and Floyd wander off together to "the library" and rejoin. Station Control (SW of East Conn): monitors - COMM RED, FOOD RED, PRINTING YELLOW. Commander's Office S of that (fixed log reader). Briefing Room S; South Connection W (Diplomatic iris hatch + slot); Robot Shop W (unwoken robot Oliver; heating chamber). Floyd fetched the medium drill bit out of the chamber (+3, score 8). South Junction N of South Conn; File Room SW is dark. Commander's Quarters E of office: safe (8000-setting dial, 12-20 numbers), log tape. Log tape: fuel cells locked in Dome storage bin, key in safe; alien craft in Docking Bay #1 with pyramid moved to Sci Sub-Module holding tank; Shady Dan in village sells modified ID cards; village entry forms need validation; stamp under bed (got it!). A menacing "Welder Number 4" approached; I fled east and it moved off.

### Commands 78-125: two deaths
Kept pressing the log reader's "More" despite "whine rises... grows louder" and it exploded on the 12.4.1900 entry (about a hull welder malfunctioning). Died, no save (UNDO off). Restarted: the start clock is now 5293 (it differs per game!), so the course differs: I used 235 at time 5452. Then I died again because I'd typed the course from the pilot seat with the hatch open ("can't reach hatch from the pilot seat"); air gushed out. I had saved just after setting the course, restored, stood, closed the hatch and sat back down in time. Docked (+5), ate goo, got the drill bit via Floyd again (+3 = 8). Lesson: SAVE often. Last log entries I heard: fuel cells in the Dome bin with the key in the safe; pyramid in the Sci Sub-Module tank; Shady Dan and village entry forms; stamp under the bed; sabotage of simple machinery; the collater and web-feeder; hull welders malfunctioning.

### Commands 126-155
Got the stamp again. Mapped the inner ring: Station Control lies between South Junction (W), the Commander's Office (S) and East Connection (NE). East Junction is W of East Connection; North Junction is NW of that; North Connection is N (Storage W, dark; PX E). PX Vendo-Matic: items cost 1 galakmid; 6 All-Purpose Timer and 9 Large Drill Bit are in stock, the rest sold out. I need a coin. Tube N leads to the Sci Sub-Module: Engineering Lab (gangways up/down) and Engineering Office N (Schmidt's diary: the pyramid is over a billion years old; the dot markings have "nonvisual properties"; "my pal, the mayor... linguistic training"). Astro Lab up (twenty-prong fromitz board, taken), Astro Office N (empty), Scientists' Quarters up top (nothing).

### Commands 156-185
Sci Sub-Module: Bio Lab (below Engineering) and Bio Office N (a bloodstained note: "think of this station as a cell and the pyramid as a mechanized bacterioph[age]"). Holding Tank Level at the bottom: the tank is blasted open and empty, so the pyramid is loose! Command Module: Level Five W = Docking Bay #2. Level Four (ladder up): Female Barracks N, SanFac SE of it, Male Barracks S (nothing in the cubicles); Docking Bay #3 W (lilac nanofilm spool, taken). Level Three: Gym N (exercise machine; sign warns about anything broadcasting on frequency 710), Laundry NW (dryer, presser, the washer missing). "Weary... find a safe place to sleep" at time ~8137.

### Commands 186-215
Level Three: Theatre S (projection booth locked), Chapel SW (puce nanofilm spool; a blinking seven-pointed star out of reach; the pulpit opens to a switch that toggles the eternal flame). Level Two (Mess Hall): a steaming coffee with nobody about (suspicious); the Food Dispensing Unit sprays ACID. Main Storage N/S of it (detonator with a blackened hyperdiode inside). Meeting Room 1 NE. Welder #4 appeared again and wandered off. Slept in a Female Barracks bed (+3, score 11), dreaming of Floyd as HAL ("I'm sorry, I can't do that"). Woke on Novem 5, clock 1652; I had dropped everything, and "take all" tried to lift Floyd too (funny).

### Commands 216-262
Auto-doors now open "sluggishly" and zoom shut: the sabotage is escalating. Level Two SE: Library (the computer terminal is removed; a voice-output spool reader). Lilac spool = "Spacetruck Refueling Instructions" (quarnum wrench... fuel cell opening); puce spool = chapel maintenance (flame fuel reservoir; a "...iode in the Chapel's star"). Both end with "You will die, human!" So the star holds a diode, perhaps to replace the detonator's blackened hyperdiode. Left the spools in the Library. Meeting Room 2 N of Library, Meeting Room 1 N of that. Carrying limit: more than 7 in hand fumbles (the game says so helpfully); dropped the diary and note in Meeting Room 2. Level One = Dome (garden, air shaft grating fixed, storage bin with new welded lock, "warm to the touch"; that's the fuel-cell bin, key in the safe).

### Commands 263-290
Elevator (a keypad; type the level number) to Level Six. Hungry again at ~2067; ate the gray goo, so only the Thermos soup is left (a food problem looms: the FDU sprays acid). Level Six: Auxiliary Barracks N and SanFac E (empty); Docking Bay #1 NW has the alien ship (empty pedestal, skeleton with an "overdeveloped tongue case", a wall of dot patterns, copied to my notes; the dots are maybe to be read aloud or by sound?); Docking Bay #4 SW (empty). S: Officers' Quarters A, Officers SanFac SE of it, Quarters C NE, Quarters B N of the SanFac; all searched, nothing. N of B: End of Corridor (a security door N with an ID reader; doors E, S, SW). Welder #2 now roams too.

### Commands 291-330
The ID card does nothing at the End of Corridor security door. Shipping Room E of it is dark. The P.A. announced a deep-space message: the Comm Center screen says "Abort assignment and return to Duffy" (the forms were found in a mislabelled pallet). Level Seven: Printing Plant (trash can with a crumpled Illegal Space Village Entry Form FW-83-Q; mauve spool = "Collater Repair Manual"). Paper Recycling Plant NW: a drill with a small bit, its motor "tired" (limited uses). Dropped the assignment form there. Stamped the village form: now validated, but still crumpled. Ominous sounds from below: clanging, a vibration of dread, a mechanical heartbeat. Theory: the pyramid is down there. Next: the form into the iris-hatch slot (maybe press it flat in the Laundry presser first).

### Commands 331-365
Level Eight's ladder is sealed from below. The crumpled form was refused by the slot ("crumpledness"); I ironed it in the Laundry presser (put it in, close, turn on, wait until steam billows, turn off, open). The South Connection slot accepted it: the hatch jammed half open (+6, score 17). Saved. The village is weightless: Grimy Passage S, Main Street (openings up, NE, S, W; SE ramps down). Travel Agency W (Welder #1 came by). Bank SE of the Travel Agency: a floating platinum detector, taken and turned on.

### Commands 366-400
Village: Greasy Straw NE of Main Street (a cup of Ramosian Fire Nectar behind the counter, NOT taken). Trading Post NE of that (sign: FREZONE explosive, "illegal wares by appointment"; an instruction sheet: put the explosive in a hole of the right diameter, attach the detonator to the explosive and a timer, set the timer, vamoose; keep it below 150 K; a twelve-prong fromitz board; I dropped the mauve spool there). Warehouse below it: a door down to an Airlock and the "Vacuum Storage Area". Opening the outer door killed me (restored). Floyd won't enter the airlock ("no room in that phone booth"). Alley SW of the Warehouse / SE of Main Street, with no exits listed. Mayor's Office up from Main Street: the textbook "Deciphering Alien Speech" with a TASTE glossary (bitter/salty/sweet/sour/bland) inside, so the alien dots are read by taste (the skeleton's big tongue case!). Loan Shark S of the Alley: a strong box with a HUGE lock. "drill lock" warned that the drill has one hole left; I didn't spend it. Saved at the Loan Shark before drilling.

## Leg handoff

### Map so far
**Duffy:** Deck Twelve (port door + slot) - aft: Forms Storage; starboard: Cargo Bay Entrance - fore: Robot Pool; starboard: Cargo Bay (spacetruck).
**Station Level 1** Dome (bin locked: fuel cells; grating). **L2** Mess Hall (acid FDU, coffee) N/S: Main Storage; NE: Meeting Rm 1 -S- Meeting Rm 2 -S- Library (SE of Mess). **L3** lobby: N Gym (freq 710 sign), NW Laundry (presser), S Theatre (booth locked), SW Chapel (star with diode, pulpit switch = flame). **L4** N Female Barracks (beds) -SE- SanFac -S- Male Barracks; W Docking Bay #3. **L5** lobby: W Docking Bay #2 (truck), N Workshop -N- Storage (dark); NE North Junction (E Sick Bay [ID door E], NE PX, N North Connection [W Storage dark, E PX, N Tube to the Sci Sub-Module]); SE South Junction (SW File Room dark, E Station Control, SE Commander's Office, S South Connection). East Junction SE of North Jct -E- East Connection (Military iris hatch + slot, S Comm Center, SW Station Control, NW Sick Bay). Commander's Office: E Quarters (safe), S Briefing Room -W- South Connection -W- Robot Shop (Oliver). **L6** N Aux Barracks/SanFac, NW Docking Bay #1 (alien ship), SW Docking Bay #4, S Officers' Quarters A-SE-SanFac-NE-C, SanFac-N-B-N-End of Corridor (N ID door, E Shipping Room dark). **L7** Printing Plant, NW Paper Recycling. **L8** sealed.
**Sci Sub-Module** (N of North Connection by Tube): Eng Lab/Office, up Astro Lab/Office, up Scientists' Quarters; down Bio Lab/Office, down Holding Tank (empty, blasted).
**Village** (S of South Connection, zero-g): Grimy Passage - Main Street (up Mayor's Office; W Travel Agency -SE- Bank -N- Main St; NE Greasy Straw -NE- Trading Post -down- Warehouse -down- Airlock -down- vacuum; Warehouse SW Alley; Main St SE Alley; Alley S Loan Shark).

### Puzzles solved
Robot Pool (form in slot, type 3 = Floyd); truck launch (both seats, activation form, course from the QX-17-T chart by the current time, CLOSE THE HATCH first); drill bit (Floyd, take drill bit: +3); stamp under the Commander's bed (log tape); sleeping in a barracks bed (+3); village entry (trash-can form, stamp it, iron it in the presser, South Connection slot: +6). Score 17/80.

### Open puzzles and theories
- Safe (Commander's Quarters) holds the Dome bin key. Theory: drill a hole (the medium or large bit gives the right diameter), put in FREZONE explosive from the vacuum storage, attach the detonator (swap the blackened hyperdiode for the chapel star's diode) and the PX timer. 
- The explosive must stay below 150 K: carry it in the Thermos? A robot may fetch it from vacuum.
- PX needs a galakmid coin (the Loan Shark strong box? the Bank?). The platinum detector may find coins or valuables.
- Security doors (Sick Bay E, End of Corridor N) need a better ID: Shady Dan's modified cards.
- Dark rooms (both Storages, the File Room, the Shipping Room) need a light.
- Alien dots are read by taste (glossary in my scratch notes); the missing pyramid is probably below on Level 8 (the heartbeat noises). Welders are menacing, and the station's machines are being sabotaged.
- Food: only the Thermos soup is left; the FDU sprays acid; the Fire Nectar is in the Greasy Straw.

### What I would try next
Explore the rest of the Alley's branches (Shady Dan?); taste the dots; use the platinum detector around the village; decide what the last drill hole is for (the safe, surely); get a coin for the PX timer and large bit; reach the chapel star (stand on the pulpit?). SAVE before every experiment: UNDO is off.

**End of leg 1:** 400/400 commands. At the Loan Shark (village), score 17/80, time 4112 on Day 2, saved there. Floyd and Plato are off playing hide-and-seek in the village. Four deaths/near-deaths so far: log reader explosion, launching with the hatch open, the airlock vacuum (restored), plus the restart.

# Leg 2

### Commands 401-425
Explored the Alley's branches: E led through a Studio (garbage "sculpture") into a Junk Yard with magnetic spaceboots. The game warned clearly that carrying them with my ID card would wipe it, so I left them for now. Up from there: Shady Dan's office, with a jerry-built keypad machine. Turned it on and put in the card ("Current rank is 6"), typed 10, "Grand Fleet HyperAdmiral". My hands were overfull, so the card-taking fumbled once; I dropped the textbook there (the glossary is in my notes). NW from Dan's = Trading Post. Hungry and thirsty again at ~4334. The platinum detector "is getting warm" in the Greasy Straw. Welder #1 lurks near the Bank.

### Commands 426-455
Drank the Thermos soup (now empty: maybe a cold carrier for the explosive). HyperAdmiral card opens Sick Bay's east door: the Brig (three locked, empty cells). It also opens the End of Corridor door on Level Six: the Armory, +5 (score 22), with a fusor-beam zapgun reading "7" (charges, I suppose). Taken. The platinum detector got "warm" then "very warm" as I walked (Greasy Straw, Level Five lobby); I switched it off, fearing it would burn. The Shipping Room is still pitch black. Heading to the Chapel to get the star's diode.

### Commands 456-485
Replayed the puce spool: nothing new (static over "...iode in the Chapel's star has an expected life of..."). Welder #2 came at me in the Library; one zapgun shot vaporised it. Chapel star: climbing the pulpit makes it sway and I fall; Floyd and Plato are both too short; throwing the kit at it says "You missed". Parked the star. Coffee in the Mess Hall is cold. Main Storage wraps round to the Mess Hall. Next: the Robot Shop, to see whether Oliver can be woken (a robot for the vacuum storage?).

### Commands 486-515
Oliver in the Robot Shop is "incubating" (2-20 days per my old robotics text), so no help yet. File Room is pitch black; "turn on light" does nothing. Station Control monitors now: COMM RED, LIFE SUPPORT YELLOW, FOOD RED, GRAVITY YELLOW, COMPUTER GREEN, POWER RED, PRINTING RED. Theory: gravity will fail and I'll float up to the chapel star. The spacetruck radio is damaged (no microphone); "tune radio to 710" = "Fat chance." With the detector back on, no warmth in the Level 5 lobby this time, so the warmth follows something that moves (or time). Back to the village to hunt a coin: the Bank, the Travel Agency, and the strong box.

### Commands 516-575
The Loan Shark's strong box: "shoot lock with zapgun" vaporised the box and left a galakmid coin (+5, 27). Airlock: closing the inner door and the Thermos first did not help; opening the lower door still killed me (restored). I need a spacesuit or a robot for the vacuum storage. A big discovery: the Trading Post's "many directions" hid a whole second quarter. N: Grocery (plastic bag of vacuum taffy, taken), N: Broadway (N Recruitment Office; NE Rec Shop with a simulation booth, flavour only; E Field Office with a miner's HEADLAMP). As I reached for the headlamp, PLATO stunned me and explained the pyramid: a Zeenak weapon that turns machines against their makers and builds replicas. Floyd, torn, knocked the gun away when I said "floyd, help"; Plato was blown apart (+7, score 34). ("floyd, help!" with the "!" was not understood.) I recalled dimly from the box that Plato turns; the game confirmed it.

### Commands 576-625
Put on and lit the headlamp; ate the vacuum taffy (hunger fixed). Mapped more village: Barbershop SE of Broadway (mirror, W to the Grocery); Saloon SE of the Grocery (E: Casino with dice and a roulette wheel, flavour so far; W back to the Trading Post). Welder #3 attacked at the Trading Post; zapped it (the gun now reads 4). Broadway W: Makeshift Connector W to East Connection, so the "Military" hatch is just a back door. Broadway SW: Pet Store with an Arcturian balloon creature (hydrogen-filled, floats in gravity). Opening the cage freed it, but grabbing the leash in zero-g makes it fart and I let go (the game hints: somewhere with gravity it would behave). Theory: in gravity it floats up and could lift/reach the chapel star. How to get it into gravity is the puzzle.

### Commands 626-660
Broadway's down exit: Fortune Teller (crystal ball with a joke "tips" message). Walked back through the East Connection to the PX, saved, put the coin in and typed 6 (timer): "klunk", nothing in the hole. Kicking/shaking/hitting it: "fails to dislodge the timer". Reaching into the hole, I feel it with my fingertips but can't grip it. Floyd's reach finds nothing ("not even a ball"). The headlamp is dimming (batteries!), so I switch it off between uses. I'm weary again (~7555). Theory for the timer: something sticky or magnetic to fish it out. I ate the vacuum taffy (sticky!) earlier, which may have been a mistake; the magnetic spaceboots are another candidate.

### Commands 661-690
Shoving the drill into the PX hole: it just drops out. Dropped my ID card in the PX (so the boots can't wipe it), saved, slept in the Female Barracks: a Resida plague dream, Novem 6, no points this time. My chronometer has STOPPED (no more time on the status line), and Floyd now kicks my mattress and swears ("kripping"): the pyramid's influence on him? Doors now barely open. Walked the back way (East Connection, Makeshift Connector, Broadway, Grocery, Trading Post, SE to Shady Dan's, down to the Junk Yard) and took the magnetic spaceboots. Now back to the PX to try them on the timer.

### Commands 691-715
Back at the PX with the boots: shoving them into the hole, they just drop out, like the drill. Hungry again. The FDU still sprays acid. I drank the cold coffee: POISONED, died, restored (fair; it had been suspicious from the start). Walked to the Greasy Straw and drank the Ramosian Fire Nectar: "thick and warming", the cup vaporised. Hunger fixed, I hope. Floyd is increasingly nasty (stomps my foot, curses my ancestors).

### Commands 716-740
Tried the bag and the boots on the balloon creature: no good; each grab makes it fart and I drop everything (the game repeats: "somewhere with gravity"). "take all" tries to take Floyd, who shoves me. Headlamp on in the dark Storage W of North Connection: it is the same room as the Workshop's north Storage. Found a JAMMER: black box, antenna, twenty tiny sockets, frequency 0-1400, set to 337. The twenty sockets surely take the twenty-prong fromitz board (left in the Library). The Gym sign warned about things broadcasting on 710: set the jammer to 710?

### Commands 741-790
Put the twenty-prong board into the jammer. The Gym sign: the exercise machine's diagnostics talk on 710, and the machine itself is GONE from the Gym (another roaming machine, like the welders?). Set the jammer to 710. File Room (lit): octuplet forms, nothing. Shipping Room: pallets of form boxes and a sign "Always return the FORKLIFT" (the forklift is missing too). Then I tried the elevator to 8: the shaft had one Gee of gravity (the warning) and the car power-dived: dead. Restored to the Workshop save and redid the board and the jammer; saved in the Library. Level 8 must be reached some other way (the ladder is sealed from below).

### Commands 791-800
Walked down to Level Seven (the mechanical heartbeat below again). The ladder to Eight is still sealed from below. Saved at the Printing Plant, then turned the jammer (710) on: "a clanging noise from the deck below. Suddenly, it stops." So the jammer affects whatever is working on Level Eight (the exercise machine / pyramid factory?). The ladder is still sealed. Leg spent.

## Leg 2 handoff

### Map additions (see leg 1 for the rest)
**Village, second quarter** (Trading Post exits): Trading Post N Grocery (N Broadway; E Barbershop via Broadway SE; SE Saloon). Saloon E Casino (dice, roulette; flavour), Saloon W Trading Post. Trading Post SE Shady Dan's (ID machine; down Junk Yard -W- Studio -W- Alley). Broadway: N Recruitment Office; NE Rec Shop (simulation booth, flavour); E Field Office; SE Barbershop; SW Pet Store (balloon creature, fixed cage; SE back to the Trading Post); W Makeshift Connector -W- East Connection (the Military hatch); down Fortune Teller (crystal ball). Broadway NW does not exist.
**Station:** Sick Bay E (HyperAdmiral card) = Brig (3 locked empty cells). End of Corridor N (card) = Armory. Storage (L5) = one room between the Workshop and North Connection. File Room and Shipping Room are lit-only flavour (forms; a "return the forklift" sign).

### Puzzles solved this leg
- Shady Dan's machine: card in slot, type 10: HyperAdmiral, opens the security doors. Armory: +5 (zapgun, 7 charges; now 4).
- Loan Shark box: shoot lock with zapgun, coin, +5.
- Plato's betrayal (Field Office, when taking the headlamp): "floyd, help" and Floyd saves you, +7. Score 34/80.
- Food: vacuum taffy (Grocery), Fire Nectar (Greasy Straw). The coffee is POISON, the FDU sprays acid.

### State at end
Printing Plant (L7), score 34, Day 3, chronometer stopped. Saved there (jammer off in that save). Wearing the magnetic boots, the headlamp (dimming: switch it off when not needed), the uniform. Carrying the jammer (board in, set to 710, ON now), the drill (small bit, ONE hole left), the empty plastic bag, the kit (stamp, medium bit, empty Thermos), the zapgun (4), the detonator (blackened hyperdiode). The ID CARD IS ON THE PX FLOOR (dropped so the boots can't wipe it): take off and drop the boots before picking it up. Floyd is sulky and increasingly rude (the pyramid's influence?). Welders #1 and #4 are still roaming.

### Open puzzles and theories
- PX timer: coin spent, "klunk", the timer is stuck. You can feel it with your fingertips but can't grip it; kicking/shaking fails; the drill and the boots put in the hole just drop out; Floyd finds nothing. Try something sticky (the taffy is eaten; more gum?), or ask Floyd again when he's in a better mood.
- Balloon creature (Pet Store): can't be held in zero-g; the hint is gravity. Maybe a use for the chapel star (it floats up in gravity?) or the flame (hydrogen!). How do I move it into gravity?
- Chapel star diode: out of reach (the pulpit sways, the robots are too short, throwing "misses").
- Level Eight: the ladder is sealed from below; the elevator is a death trap (it dives). The jammer at 710 stops the clanging below. Perhaps the exercise machine / forklift are down there.
- Vacuum storage (explosive): the airlock kills without a suit, and Floyd won't come.
- Safe: drill (last hole), explosive, detonator with a good diode, timer. The diode from the star.

### What I would try next
Turn the jammer on/off near other places (the Gym, the elevator?) and watch; return to the PX with Floyd in a good mood; look for a spacesuit (Dan's used-ship lot?); try the balloon from the Makeshift Connector boundary.

# Leg 3

Started with --new-leg at the Printing Plant (L7), score 34, jammer on (710). Plan: see what the jammer changed below, then the PX timer, the balloon, the star.

### Commands 801-830
Checked Level Eight: still sealed. The elevator now power-dives to death on ANY descent (tried 8, then 5; restored twice); the shaft has 1 G. So I walk the ladders from now on. Zapped Welder #4 in the Pet Store. The balloon creature still farts me into dropping everything; pushing it does nothing, the leash can't be tied, and Floyd wants to play hide-and-seek, not help. In the Dome, the grating is "securely affixed"; I zapped it foolishly (a funny footnote chain, but the gun is down to 2). Theory: the safe needs a hole of the right size for FREZONE from vacuum storage, so I need a spacesuit. Hunting one in the village (Recruitment Office, Travel Agency).

### Commands 831-870
Recruitment Office and Travel Agency: flavour only, no spacesuit. The airlock: closing the upper door then opening the lower kills (lungs rupture); restored. Stencil: "SECURE ALL OPEN CONTAINERS BEFORE DEPRESSURIZATION" (the Thermos? the bag?). Floyd won't go down or fetch. Field Office: the platinum detector (which I'd left there) is TOO HOT to pick up while on: something platinum near here? Turned it off; no room to carry it (the bag is too small). Spacetruck: nothing new. Hungry again and no food source known. Level Eight ladder still sealed. New theory: the balloon creature as a parachute down the (now 1 G) elevator shaft to Level Eight, if I can ever get it into gravity.

### Commands 871-995: starvation, forced restart
Theatre booth: locked. Oliver: still incubating. Hunger came back hard ("ravenous"). The FDU sprays acid (the jammer at 337, 710 or off makes no difference). Main Storage's "organic materials" are not food; the Dome plants are "not edible"; the Grocery shelves hold nothing. I wasted ten commands typing directions in Main Storage (its exits are NW/SW). Collapsed in the Grocery; restore only brings back the latest save (already ravenous in the Mess Hall), and typed RESTORE can't choose an older one. With every meal I found (two goos, soup, taffy, nectar) eaten by Day 3, the game is unwinnable, so I RESTART from the opening. Lesson for the replay: be MUCH faster, and hunt for food supplies early.

### Commands 996-1030: the replay
Restarted (new clock 4869). Noticed the Robot Pool also offers Rex (heavy lifting) and Helen (form bursting); I took Floyd again. Launched at 5090 with course 343 (hatch closed first), docked, +5; hungry on arrival, ate the orange goo. Floyd fetched the drill bit (+3, 8) and told me touchingly that he'd like to teach Oliver paddleball when Oliver wakes. Stamp under the Commander's bed. Next: fromitz board, the trash-can form, the presser, the village; food carefully rationed this time.

### Commands 1031-1075
Twenty-prong board from the Astro Lab. The Military hatch is shut this early. Plato joined at the North Junction. Trash-can form taken and stamped, drill taken, assignment form dropped. Laundry: the WASHER is missing too (like the exercise machine and forklift: machines being taken to Level Eight?). Pressed the form. Detonator from Main Storage. The FDU sprays acid even this early, so it's not a late sabotage. Off to the village.

### Commands 1076-1160
Village hatch opened (+6, 14). Shady Dan: card to rank 10. Taffy bag, headlamp (Plato did NOT betray me this time: it must be timed, not triggered by the headlamp). The Military hatch is frozen open from this side, so the Makeshift Connector route works. Jammer plus board, set to 710. At the Armory door, Welder #3 killed me while I fumbled the card (ignored two warnings, my fault); restored to the Field Office and redid it. Armory +5 (19). The carry limit forced me to leave the detonator in the Armory. Weary at ~8130, so to bed next.

### Commands 1161-1200

# Playtest diary: r10-click-fullA

- **Mode:** click
- **Start:** the start of the game
- **Persona:** a game-design student who narrates theories aloud and experiments with every object
- **Seed:** 29514
- **Conveniences:** on
- **Undo:** off
- **Build commit:** d330802
- **Budget:** about 400 commands per leg, 1500 commands in all
- **Round:** 10
- **Friction log:** filed through the harness (--friction), in playtests/2026-09-27/r10-click-fullA.friction.jsonl

## Narrative

**Cmds 0.** Starting at Deck Twelve with three forms, an ID card, a chronometer. Theory: the forms act as keys, so bureaucracy is the puzzle gate. There's a slot by the port door, so the ID card probably goes in it.

**Cmds 1-23.** The Forms Storage room is only flavour. The ID card in the Deck Twelve slot just gets spat back, so the port door stays shut. At the Robot Pool I fed in the Robot Use form, and bin 3 turned out to be Floyd, so I typed 3. In the Cargo Bay spacetruck I took the survival kit (orange goo, gray goo, Thermos). The activation form needs both seats filled; Floyd took the copilot seat by himself. The course comes from the time:course table on form QX-17-T. At time ~5317 I typed 272, and the game said "Course set." Theory: the hatch closes by itself at launch.

**Cmds 24-48.** DIED: the truck launched with the hatch open and all the air went out. That was my fault, but I got no warning, and the seated menu still offered Close. I restarted and replayed; this time I closed the hatch before sitting, typed course 272 at time ~5344, and SAVED. Waiting about 6 times took me through the trip to the station, and docking gave +5 (score 5). I was hungry, so I ate the orange goo (apricot yogurt!). Now I'm in the Level Five lobby: there's an elevator, a ladder up and down, and exits N, NE, SE and W (the dock). No one came to meet me. Spooky. Theory: the station is abandoned and something went wrong here.

**Cmds 49-68.** Explored Level Five. The Workshop (N of the lobby) had a twenty-ohm bedistor, which I took. North of it, Storage is pitch black and I need a light. NE is North Junction; E of that is Sick Bay, whose security door ID reader ignores my card. East Connection has a sealed iris hatch with a slot (the Military Sub-Module). The Comm Center beacon button shocks you, so it's sabotaged. The Station Control board shows COMMUNICATION RED, FOOD RED, PRINTING YELLOW. The Commander's Office has a fixed log reader but no tape. Theory: find the commander's log tape to learn what happened, and get a commander's ID for the security doors.

**Cmds 69-100.** Commander's Quarters: took a log tape from the desk; the safe has an 8000-setting dial and a 12–20 number combination. Played the tape in the office reader, pushing the red button for each More. Clues: the fuel cells are locked in the Dome storage bin and the key is in the safe; Shady Dan in the village sells modified ID cards; the validation stamp is under the bed. The alien pyramid was moved to the Sci Sub-Module holding tank, and machines are breaking down (sabotage?). I looked under the bed, got the STAMP, and then the log reader EXPLODED, just as the log foreshadowed. In the Briefing Room, hull Welder #4 came at me "with excitement", so I fled. Theory: the pyramid is corrupting machines, and Floyd may be at risk later. Saved.

**Cmds 101-118.** South Junction (a ring corridor) leads SW to the File Room, which is dark. South Connection has a Diplomatic iris hatch with a slot. Met Plato, a gentle librarian robot; the Ask topics are limited to visible objects, which frustrated me. The Robot Shop has Oliver, a newborn robot not yet awake, which Floyd found touching, and a heating chamber with a drill bit. I told Floyd to take the bit (+3, score 8). Welder #4 keeps stalking me, but moving away makes it retreat. North Connection leads N to the Sci Sub-Module, W to Storage (dark), and E to the PX. The PX vendo sells an All-Purpose Timer and a Large Drill Bit at 1 galakmid each, but I have no coin. Sleepy in ~84 moves.

**Cmds 119-150.** Science Sub-Module, which has 5 levels. Engineering Office: Schmidt's diary. The pyramid is about a billion years old and came from another galaxy; the wall dots have 'nonvisual properties' (braille-like?), and "the mayor" has linguistic training. Astro Lab: a twenty-prong fromitz board, taken. Bio Office note: "think of the station as a cell and the pyramid as a mechanized bacteriophage", with blood stains. The holding tank at the bottom was blasted open and is empty, so the pyramid is loose and hijacking machines. Welder #3 appeared too. Slept in the Scientists' Quarters (+3, score 11); I woke on Day 2 with everything dropped, and Take all worked (Floyd is too heavy to lift, lol).

**Cmds 151-190.** The Thermos holds blue soup, kept for later. The ladder goes up from Level Five. Level Four has the Female and Male Barracks and a SanFac, plus Docking Bay #3 with a lilac nanofilm spool (taken). The auto-doors are now 'sluggish' and slam shut early, so machines are going bad; I'm worried a door will crush someone. Level Three: the Gym exercise machine has a sign warning not to bring anything broadcasting on frequency 710 near it (a puzzle hook?). The Theatre has a projection booth with a lock. The Laundry has no washer (the missing washer is suspicious), plus a dryer and presser, both empty. The Chapel has an eternal flame, a blinking seven-pointed star out of reach, a pulpit hiding a flame switch, and a puce nanofilm spool (taken). Ate the gray goo when hungry ("not hungry yet" blocks early eating). Plato and Floyd went off to the library.

**Cmds 191-228.** Level Two is the Mess Hall (cold coffee, food units). N/S lead to Main Storage, which has a DETONATOR; opened, it holds a blackened hyperdiode. NE goes to Meeting Room 1, then Meeting Room 2, then the Library, whose nanofilm reader plays the spools. Lilac: spacetruck fuel-cell replacement "with the quarnum wrench". Puce: chapel maintenance, where the Chapel star has a (hyper)diode. Both dissolve into "You will die, human!" Chilling, and a great touch. The ladder top is the DOME, with the locked, WARM storage bin (fuel cells; the key is in the commander's safe) and an air shaft grating. Took the elevator (keypad = level number) down to 5. The Comm Center screen: the Duffy found the forms, "Abort assignment and return." LOL. Theory: to go home I need the fuel cells (bin key from the safe) and a quarnum wrench. Also: take the chapel star's hyperdiode to fix the detonator.

**Cmds 229-266.** Level Six: Auxiliary Barracks and SanFac; Docking Bay #1 holds the ALIEN SHIP (empty pedestal, skeleton, dots). TASTING the dots gives a taste-language message (saved in my scratch dots.txt); the mayor can read it. Docking Bay #4 is empty. Officers' Quarters A/B/C and SanFac. End of Corridor has another security door (ID reader), and the Shipping Room (E) is dark. Level Seven, the Printing Plant: a trash can with a crumpled Illegal Space Village Entry Form FW-83-Q. I VALIDATED it with the stamp (no points; I heard a mechanical heartbeat below). Took a mauve spool. The Paper Recycling Plant (NW) had a DRILL with a small bit. Theory: the drill opens the safe or the theatre booth lock, and the village form goes in the South Connection (Diplomatic) slot.

**Cmds 267-297.** The drill 'may not have much work left in it', so it's limited-use and I'm saving it. The Printing Plant ladder down to Level 8 is sealed from below (the pyramid's lair?), with clanging and throbbing from underneath; elevator 8 won't move. At the South Connection slot the crumpled form was rejected ("crumpledness"), so I used the laundry presser (put in, close, turn on, open) to get a neatly ironed form. In the slot, the hatch half-irises open (+6, score 17). Went through the Grimy Passage (weightless) to Main Street in the village: deserted, with exits up, down, NE, S, W, SE. Floyd and Plato stayed behind.

**Cmds 298-325.** Village: W is the Travel Agency, then SE the Bank, where I took the platinum detector (now on; hoping it finds a coin for the PX). NE of Main Street is the Greasy Straw (cup of Ramosian Fire Nectar behind the counter; Welder #1 showed up), then the Trading Post: a sign saying FREZONE explosive is available, a twelve-prong fromitz board, and an instruction sheet (insert the explosive in a hole, attach detonator and timer, set the timer; keep it below 150 K). Below the Trading Post, the Warehouse has a vacuum storage airlock ("trespassers will be spaced"). Then the Alley (Missionary N, Junk Yard E) and the Junk Yard's magnetic boots; the port WARNED me they'd wipe my ID card. Nice. Dropped the survival kit, kept the Thermos, and ate the blue soup. Up from the Junk Yard is SHADY DAN's, where the machine re-ranked my ID card to 10, Grand Fleet HyperAdmiral (max is 10). Saved.

**Cmds 326-360.** The Grocery has a plastic bag of vacuum taffy (left it there). Broadway leads N to the Recruitment Office and NE to the Rec Shop (simulation booths). Up from Main Street is the MAYOR'S OFFICE: a textbook 'Deciphering Alien Speech' with a glossary slip. Decoded the dots: "Hunji brethren: sabotage failed; however I have shined light upon the Zeenak weapon's solitary weakness: Element 78 [PLATINUM]! Turn back the deadly radiations! The air is souring." Wow. The Military hatch at East Connection is now frozen open onto the Makeshift Connector, which leads to Broadway, the village's second link. The platinum detector said 'getting warm' as I entered East Connection. The HyperAdmiral ID opens the Sick Bay security door; it leads to the Brig (3 empty cells), and the door nearly nipped my heels on the way out. Saved.

**Cmds 361-390.** The HyperAdmiral ID opened the End of Corridor security door (Level 6) into the ARMORY (+5, score 22); took the fusor-beam zapgun (indicator reads 7). Dropped the stamp and mauve spool in the Armory. In the Theatre the platinum detector says 'getting VERY warm', so the platinum is probably inside the locked projection booth. The drill with the small bit fails, and so does the medium bit ('The point of the drill doesn't seem to be as hard as the lock'). The zapgun on the lock: 'glows then cools' (one charge wasted). Security and auto-doors now 'almost nip your heels'.

## New issues

| Issue | Title | Area / room | Kind | Rows this round | Rows in all | Rounds | Suggested | Norm confirms | Status | Evidence |

| SF-212 | Round 10 vocabulary: "paths" (the Dome's pebbled paths) and "level" (Level Five, Level Eight) | Parser / Dome | parse | 2 | 2 | 10 | A | A | open | D28 item 6, the standing rule. Printed: "Pebbled paths" (the Dome, station.zil 2056; also 2034, 2037), "Level" in every lobby name (station.zil 25, 1115, 1199, 2224) and "Level Eight" (station.zil 2684, 3761, 3879). Oracle, route step 29 + SEARCH PATHS, EXAMINE PATH, EXAMINE PEBBLES, ASK FLOYD ABOUT LEVEL EIGHT, ASK FLOYD ABOUT EIGHT: each gives [I don't know the word "...."], and our engine says the same. Add, with the conveniences on (rules/library.js, the conveniences vocabulary beside SPOTLIGHTS-PSEUDO): PATHS and PATH as Dome scenery, with PEBBLED an adjective. LEVEL as a topic word with the number words as adjectives (as MAYOR in SF-127), so ASK X ABOUT LEVEL EIGHT gets the robot's stock answer and EXAMINE LEVEL a plain refusal. Rows: r10-typed-full#7, #33. |
| SF-213 | Typed "floyd, help!": [I don't know the word "help!."] (a trailing exclamation mark) | Parser / Field Office | parse | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | C | left | The original. Oracle, route step 29 + FLOYD, HELP!: [I don't know the word "help!."], and ours matches. The V3 dictionary does not split on "!", so it stays on the word; the refusal costs no turn (the row says so). Not a word the game prints, so outside D28 item 6. The click entry "Help!" is ours (SF-185), and the harness already drops its closing punctuation. Kept. Row: r10-typed-full#13. |
| SF-214 | Typed RESTORE always loads the newest of the ten kept saves; only the page's Restore… can choose an older one | Page / Loan Shark | blocked | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | A | open | Ours. The 1987 RESTORE asked the interpreter for a file (V-RESTORE, verbs.zil 48-60, with V-SAVE at 31), so a typed player could pick any save. Our V_RESTORE (rules/library.js:341) loads the newest of the ten kept (SF-013, KEEP_SAVES), and only the page's Restore... list (wwwroot/ui, the quick row's Restore..., about line 175) picks another. r10-typed-full had all ten saves starving by command 971; RESTORE AIRLOCK got [That sentence isn't one I recognize.] (973), so the run restarted from the opening at 994. SF-013 held (ten kept, the replaced one named each time); this is its typed half. Fix, interface only: with more than one kept position, typed RESTORE lists them numbered and takes the choice ("RESTORE 3", or a number at the prompt), as the 1987 file prompt did; the harness's typed mode prints the same list. Row: r10-typed-full#23. |
| SF-215 | The Theatre's projection booth is "closed and locked", and nothing opens it (drill, zapgun and examine all fail) | Station / Theatre | confusing | 3 | 3 | 10 | B | C | left | The original, a red herring. PROJECTION-BOOTH-F answers OPEN, ENTER, WALK-TO and SEARCH with "The projection booth is closed and locked." and LOOK-INSIDE with blackness, and nothing else (station.zil 1656-1660). The booth is a PSEUDO with no lock object; the Theatre's LOCK is the Brig's pseudo, BRIG-LOCK-F (station.zil 1650). EXAMINE on a PSEUDO is "Totally ordinary looking ..." (V-EXAMINE, verbs.zil 841-843), and the drill's "point ... not as hard as" is V-DRILL's own refusal (verbs.zil 644). The detector's warmth there is its own overheating clock (I-PLATINUM-DETECTOR, interrupts.zil 70-83), not the booth. Kept. Rows: r10-typed-full#27, r10-click-fullA#14, r10-click-fullB#7 (whose 32-millichron examine is SF-108). |
| SF-216 | WAIT UNTIL more than 40 ahead: "That's too long to wait.", and WAIT <number> is not understood | Parser / Chapel | tedious | 1 | 1 | 10 | B | C | left | The original. WAIT UNTIL <n> works only 1 to 40 ahead and WAIT FOR <n> only up to 40; anything else is "That's too long to wait." (INTNUM-F, globals.zil 122-132). A plain WAIT is 40 millichrons (V-WAIT, verbs.zil 2449-2455), and there is no WAIT <number> syntax (syntax.zil 617-620). Oracle, route step 29 + WAIT UNTIL 4800 (at 6755): "That's too long to wait."; ours matches. Kept. Row: r10-typed-full#29. |
| SF-217 | Harness: a phrase with part of a thing's name ("take fromitz board") is refused, though the sent words ("take board") and the full name work | Harness / Astro Lab | parse | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | A | open | Harness only (the page has no phrases). A click-mode phrase matches an entry's sent words, its label, or "<entry> <the thing's full label>" (scripts/playtest.mjs:299-310). "take fromitz board" is none of them (sent "take board", thing "twenty-prong fromitz board"), so it was refused at no cost (transcript, before command 123). Fix: also take "<entry> <a trailing part of the thing's name>" when it names one thing on screen (scripts/playtest.mjs:305-307). Row: r10-click-fullA#8. |
| SF-218 | The platinum detector: TAKE says "too hot to pick up", but TURN OFF's implied take picks it up | Village / North Junction | bug | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | C | left | The original. TURN OFF is (TAKE) (syntax.zil 593). The parser's implied take calls ITAKE directly (ITAKE-CHECK, parser.zil 1716-1727) and never runs PLATINUM-DETECTOR-F's TAKE clause, the only place "too hot to pick up" is said (village.zil 1052-1056). The detector has no TRYTAKEBIT (village.zil 1041), so the implied take goes ahead. The oracle run could not reach counter 100 without a welder killing the player (two tries); the ZIL path is unambiguous. Kept. Row: r10-click-fullA#15. |
| SF-219 | Click menus: Wear vanishes from a thing's menu while the player carries too much (the space suit), so D28's load line and hint never show | Click menus / Trading Post | confusing | 1 | 1 | 10 | B | A | open | Ours. A menu offers only entries whose words dry-parse (engine/zmenus.js menuItems via textFor; findOffer, 585-606). Over the weight limit, WEAR SUIT's implied take fails (ITAKE, rules/library.js:1605-1611), so Wear drops out of the suit's menu without a word. SF-129's load line and D12's hint, written for exactly this case, then never show in click mode. Reproduced headless: route step 242 (the Flophouse, 12 things carried), the suit's menu is Examine, Take, More...; at step 245 (three dropped) it is Examine, Take, Wear, More.... Take stayed, and its refusal helped (the row). Fix, interface only: keep Wear on a WEARBIT thing not held wherever Take is offered, so the refusal and its hint explain (engine/zmenus.js, the textFor filter). Row: r10-click-fullA#31 (transcript 1049-1053). |
| SF-220 | Harness: Restore… numbers: a refused bare number names the Save… menu, and "<Restore> <number>" fails for a position not yet numbered | Harness / Dome | confusing | 2 | 2 | 10 | B | A | open | Harness only. (1) The tester opened Restore... (6) at command 1202, took a turn (1203, which closes it), then answered 38. The closed-menu refusal names the first menu the number is found in, and a saved position shares its number between Save over and Restore (SF-171; scripts/playtest.mjs:201-205, 283-287), so it named the Save... menu and the tester feared an overwrite. Nothing was overwritten: "6 38" then restored the Dome. (2) At 1245, "6 17" was refused. The Bottom of Air Shaft position had been saved over at 1220, so it gets a number only when a menu lists it (numberOf), while the SF-097 path matches with known() (scripts/playtest.mjs:316-318), which is empty until it is printed. The printed menu then showed 17, and "17" worked (1246). Fix: for a saved position, the closed-menu refusal names the Restore entry (or both); "<menu> <number>" numbers the menu's children (numberOf) before matching. Rows: r10-click-fullA#32, #33. |
| SF-221 | Harness: a door shared by two rooms has different numbers in each (the inner airlock door: 44 Close in the Warehouse, 44 Examine in the Airlock) | Harness / Airlock | confusing | 1 | 1 | 10 | B | A | open | Harness only. A door's node is keyed door:<id> in the room's own pool (scripts/lib/playtest-surface.mjs:84-86; scripts/playtest.mjs:199-200, where thingKey takes only obj: and inv:), so its entries are numbered per room. The inner airlock door was 40 in both rooms, but Open was 43 in the Warehouse (command 1442), and Examine 44 and Close 45 in the Airlock (1445-1446): "40 44" examined instead of closing, a wasted turn. Fix: number a door and its entries from the things' pool, keyed by the door and the verb, so a door shared by two rooms keeps its numbers in both. Row: r10-click-fullA#36. |
| SF-222 | Shooting a welder while carrying the explosive sublimes it (the only one); the zap gives no warning | Village / Barbershop | blocked | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | C | left | The original. WELDER-F on SHOOT: if the explosive is VISIBLE, "As the heat wave hits the explosive, it suddenly sublimes into a puff of FREZONE (tm) gas." and it is removed (globals.zil 1257-1266). The D28 backstop named it at once: "(The game can no longer be won: the explosive has sublimed away in the heat, and there was only the one. ...)" (transcript command 1464). The tester calls it fair but harsh. A warning on the zap would be a deviation, and a fast informed loss stays under D28 item 4. Kept. Row: r10-click-fullA#38. |
| SF-223 | Tell Floyd to… has no direction orders: the player wanted to send Floyd through the airlock alone | Robots / Warehouse | blocked | 1 | 1 | 10 | A | C | left | The original. FLOYD-F answers any direction order with "Floyd looks slightly embarrassed. 'You know Floyd and his sense of direction.' ... 'Tell Floyd a story?'" (ship.zil 417-421), and at the airlock he says he will wait above (interrupts.zil 276-285). D15: the Tell menu lists the orders FLOYD-F acts on, and a walk order only gets that refusal. The vac yard is the player's job. Kept. Row: r10-click-fullB#38. |

(the Brig lock and cells, the grating, the shaft), so puzzle and scenery read alike | Station / Brig | confusing | 1 | 1 | 10 | B | C | left | The original. V-EXAMINE says "Totally ordinary looking <thing>." for every PSEUDO and, 35% of the time, for a thing with nothing else to say (verbs.zil 841-843). The Brig's cells and lock and the shaft are such words. A real puzzle object says more on EXAMINE; that is how the 1987 game tells them apart. Kept (D15: Examine is on every scenery word). Row: r10-click-fullB#41. |
